hero.title: A personal AI workbench, *running on real Claude Code*
hero.lede: PHẢN-TỈNH started as a reflection skill: separate fact, emotion, ego and structure so you act with a clearer head. Today it is a personal web app with 52 modules, spanning reflection, languages, research, decisions and economics. It uses no API key. Every chat session is a real Claude Code TUI in tmux on the host machine, and every one-shot run is a `claude -p` call that returns JSON matching a schema. This page goes from the product overview down to each flow and each table.

sections.title: What the product is
sections.intro: A reflection and systems-thinking app for one person, using Claude Code as its brain instead of an API key.

blocks.text:
The README describes itself: *“A personal reflection & systems-thinking app. Each chat session is bound 1:1 to a real Claude Code TUI session running in tmux on your host; the PWA is the structured front end, your terminal is the live observer.”*

The original requirements (`phantinh-requirement.md`) set a few constraints that shape the whole architecture:

- **No API key.** Every AI turn must run through the Claude Code CLI that is already logged in on the machine. The web is a structured shell in front of the terminal.
- **No login.** Skip sign-in and go straight to the dashboard. There is no user table; learning profiles are one-to-one with a Module.
- **Everything is stored in the DB.** Each business flow starts from a question or pain point and ends in a report.
- **Installable as a PWA**, opened with a hotkey (later, Raycast).

blocks.text: The web never talks to a model. It talks to **a real Claude Code terminal**, typing into tmux and reading back the JSONL transcript Claude writes itself. Almost every architectural decision downstream follows from that choice.

sections.title: Cross-cutting features
sections.intro: Things no single module owns that every module uses.

head: Feature
What it does
rows: `/history` gathers every run. Each module's history opens in a drawer, which can grow into a popup or its own page by URL.
A “take-note” button mid-chat runs a one-shot over the transcript with the module's own schema.
Each run keeps a structured payload and markdown. PDFs are built with pandoc on the host and fall back to markdown. Decisions, plans and research have `/print` routes.
One run can start another, e.g. etymology → illustration. At most 3 levels; automatic runs never overwrite an existing file.
A shared taxonomy with Unicode-aware slugs; AI tags research and decisions.
Lunar–solar birth data for the metaphysics modules; a page to assign runs that have no person.
IPA and macOS `say` through the bridge; the voice catalog is managed in admin.
`/admin/settings` has 7 tabs: modules, categories, ai agent, voice, bridge, credentials, infra. `/admin/sessions` bulk-closes, deletes and reconciles tmux with the DB.
`/admin/performance`: model / proxy / ingest / tool time per turn, tokens, cache hits. Cost is deliberately not tracked, because the app runs on a subscription plan.
`/knowledge` ingests Claude-ecosystem sources by trust tier, through 5 validation gates, into “points”.
Inside lessons: a study assistant that can call tools, with a bounded number of rounds. On every other page: a guide that returns links to the right module, after private values are masked.
Login status per Claude/Codex config directory, sync between them, sign-in from the web.

sections.title: The architecture at a glance
sections.intro: Five layers from the person to the AI agent. Each lower layer does something the one above cannot.

blocks.caption: The core API is the centre: it holds the Module catalog, runs the engines and writes to two stores. Anything that touches the host machine goes through layer 4.
blocks.ascii:
1 Surfaces     PWA · Raycast · Terminal (tmux attach -r)
      |
2 Web edge     Next.js :7777  (/api/gql proxy, /raycast/*)
      |
3 Core API     Django + Strawberry GraphQL :8888 — Postgres · Redis
      |
4 Host bridge  host-shim :9876 → phantinh-bridge (bash)
      |
5 AI agents    claude TUI in tmux · claude -p / codex exec

head: Layer
Technology
Why it is here
rows: Three ways into one system; the terminal is for watching only.
Same-origin proxy for HTTP; the only place with authentication (the Raycast token).
Django 5, Strawberry GraphQL, Pydantic, Postgres 16, Redis 7
Catalog, engines, storage. Redis holds live state, Postgres holds durable state.
Docker Desktop on macOS will not let a container use the host's tmux unix socket.
No API key: use the CLIs that are already logged in.

blocks.title: Named patterns
blocks.text: The project's architecture skill names them: **Server-Driven UI** (dispatch variant: the server declares a `kind`, the client looks up a component), **Atomic Design** (pure atoms → workflows → thin route shells), and the catalog vocabulary of **Backstage**.

sections.title: Deployment: host and Docker
sections.intro: What runs in containers, what must run on the Mac, and why.

blocks.caption: The API in Docker calls `host-shim` on the host over HTTP; the shim runs `phantinh-bridge`, which drives tmux and `claude`. The browser opens its WebSocket straight to :8888 because the Next dev server does not proxy WebSockets.
blocks.ascii:
HOST (macOS, process-compose)
  Next.js :7777   host-shim 127.0.0.1:9876 → phantinh-bridge → tmux → claude TUI
                                                     └→ claude -p / codex exec
  keychain, git, pandoc, say, ebook files, JSONL transcripts
            ^ HTTP host.docker.internal:9876
DOCKER
  api (uvicorn) :8888   db Postgres :5555   redis :6666
  api-reaper (600s)  api-sync (3600s)  api-mustwin (30s)

sections.title: A module is data
sections.intro: A new module of an existing kind needs only data. Only a new kind needs code.

blocks.caption: YAML seeds once; after that the Module row in the DB is the source of truth. The row's `kind` picks the workflow on the web and the engine in the API.
blocks.ascii:
modules/*.yaml --seed_modules (insert-only)--> Module row (DB) <-- /admin/settings
                                     | kinds.py checks keys + links
            +------------------------+------------------------+
   WEB: WORKFLOW_BY_KIND[kind]                API: engine by kind
        workflow (state + GraphQL)                 tui_chat (20) · oneshot (19)
        atoms (pure, props only)                   13 bespoke kinds

blocks.title: Main Module fields
rows: JSON whose shape the kind decides
for `tui_chat`: the skill and the opening command
the output contract and how it renders

items: **The DB is the source of truth.** `seed_modules` only inserts, so admin edits survive; `--force` re-upserts (destructive). Agents, sources and voices follow the same pattern.

**`kinds.py` is the kind manifest.** Each kind declares its valid keys and JSON types, its AI-block pairs (prompt + schema), and its links to other modules. The checks are structural only; the rules inside each section stay with that section's parser.
**Three doors run the checks:** admin save (which refuses only problems the edit itself introduces), `seed_modules`, and `check_schemas`.
**`ROLES` is the only place code names a module by id:** `business_report`, `image_follow_up` → `image_gen`, `knowledge_impact`, `must_win_goal`. The web reads them through the `moduleRoles` query.
**The two kind lists always match:** an API test compares `KINDS` with `ModuleKind`; a host-side bats test compares `ModuleKind` with the web's `MODULE_KINDS`.
**Slots and the query registry:** module config picks atoms by name (`slots`) and registered GraphQL documents by name (`queries`), never carrying code or query text.

sections.title: The TUI chat flow
sections.intro: A message goes out by pasting into tmux; the reply comes back by reading the JSONL transcript Claude writes itself.

blocks.caption: Outbound and inbound are separate. The tailer writes two places for every event: Redis for live viewers, Postgres so a page reload is still complete.
blocks.ascii:
OUTBOUND: Browser sendMessage → api (Message row) → host-shim POST /run → bridge send (paste-buffer) → claude TUI
                                                                                          | writes
INBOUND:  Browser ← graphql-ws subscription ← tailer ← bridge tail (tail -F → NDJSON) ← JSONL
                                               ├→ Redis publish phantinh.session.<id>
                                               └→ Postgres: Message, Report, jsonl_cursor

items.title: createSession
items.text: Build the opening (static, or a template + profile), create a PROVISIONING row

items.title: bridge spawn
items.text: `tmux new-session`, wait for the TUI's session UUID (up to 15 s), paste the opening, find the JSONL file

items.title: ACTIVE
items.text: Store the tmux name, session id, JSONL path, attach command; start the tailer

items.title: sendMessage
items.text: A USER row, then `bridge send` pastes into the pane + Enter

items.title: tail
items.text: Each JSONL line becomes an event: `turn_started`, `turn_event` (text, tool_use, tool_result, thinking), `turn_complete`

items.title: tailer
items.text: Publish to Redis, write Message, Report (if there is a YAML report block), TurnLatency; only then advance the cursor

items.title: sessionStream
items.text: The subscription reads Redis pub/sub and pushes 4 chunk types over graphql-ws

items.title: The cursor advances only after the writes land
fields: `jsonl_cursor` moves only after side effects succeed, and only forward.

The API reloads mid-turn 7. The next subscribe sees an ACTIVE row with no tailer, calls `ensure_tailer`, and reads again from the stored cursor. Every write is idempotent, so no message is duplicated.

items.title: Tools that block on a human are disabled
fields: Every TUI session runs with `--disallowedTools "AskUserQuestion ExitPlanMode"`.

If Claude asked through AskUserQuestion, that turn would end in `tool_use`, not `end_turn`, and would not reach the JSONL until someone answered in the TUI. The web would show your message with no reply, and the session would sit ACTIVE forever.

items.title: The report travels inside the reply
fields: The skill prints a ```` ```yaml ```` block marked `---phan-tinh-report---`. The bridge lifts it out as `report_block`; the API checks it against `report_schema` and renders markdown.
A free-form chat still ends in a structured report you can store and print.

sections.title: The one-shot flow
sections.intro: One prompt in, one schema-valid JSON out. Every door (web form, lenses, follow-ups, business reports, Raycast) goes through one engine.

items.title: prepare(RunSpec)
items.text: Check kind, mode, inputs against the schema, provider, profile — before any row exists

items.title: create_row
items.text: A PROVISIONING row with the full lineage; hold a Redis lease

items.title: run
items.text: Wait on the shared semaphore (3 at a time), build the prompt with `$`-substitution

items.title: bridge oneshot
items.text: `claude -p --json-schema … --output-format json`, prompt on stdin

items.title: Store
items.text: Re-check the payload, render markdown, write Report + `run_meta`, extract learning points, CLOSED

items.title: Follow-up
items.text: Optional: start a child run, at most 3 levels

blocks.note: `oneshot/engine.py` is the only place a one-shot run is created, executed, failed or retried; a test guards that boundary.

blocks.caption: Run profiles: the CLI's permissions are set by code, not by config
head: Profile
claude flags
Used for
rows: Image generation with codex, unattended agents
blocks.note: Every profile except `agent` also runs with `--safe-mode` (no skills, CLAUDE.md, hooks or connectors) and `--strict-mcp-config`. Extra args from a module or from settings pass an allowlist: only `--model`, `--effort` and `--append-system-prompt`, plus `--add-dir` under `agent`. Anything else is refused by the bridge with `PROFILE_FLAG_OVERRIDE`.

blocks.title: Timeout stack, all derived from PT_ONESHOT_TIMEOUT_S
rows: 600 s — kills the whole process group, returns `TIMEOUT`
blocks.note: Each outer layer waits longer than the inner one, so the error always comes from the layer that knows the cause best.

items.title: A lease for a reaper in another container
fields: Redis key `phantinh.oneshot.lease.<id>`, TTL 180 s, refreshed every 60 s. The reaper closes a PROVISIONING row only once its lease has expired.

A research run takes 8 minutes. The reaper runs every 10 minutes and sees a PROVISIONING row older than 5 minutes, but the lease is alive, so it skips it. If Redis does not answer, the reaper skips every one-shot row that tick.

items.title: The render contract
fields: Every field substituted into a template must be `required` in the schema; modules without modes may substitute only scalar values.

`safe_substitute` leaves `$name` in place when a field is missing, and prints a list as a Python repr. The test found 33 violations, all fixed; the fix is a pre-rendered “twin” field such as `corrections_markdown`.

pandoc + xelatex, return the PDF as base64
Read the outline or a page range of a PDF/EPUB

TUI printed no session id in 15 s
Transcript not found
tmux is gone

Over 600 s

legend.text: The API handles it (closes the session, tells the user)

blocks.note: Every failure is `{"kind":"bridge_error","code":…}`; the facade turns it into `BridgeInvocationError(code, detail)`.

items.title: host-shim.py
items.text: A standard-library HTTP server with 3 endpoints: `POST /run` runs one bridge command, `POST /tail` streams chunked NDJSON, `GET /health`. A POST must be `application/json` (so a foreign web page is stopped at the preflight) and carry a local Host, or a Bearer `PT_HOST_SHIM_TOKEN` when one is set; without a token it refuses to bind anything but loopback. The token is not passed down to the bridge. It writes a pidfile; the readiness probe compares the serving pid with the pidfile to catch a stale shim holding the port.

items.title: One shared event contract
items.text: `shared/protocol` defines the Pydantic event union and the Redis channel name for both the bridge and the API. The Python `RunProfile` must match `_profiles.sh`; a bats test checks it.

sections.title: Data model
sections.intro: One `models.py`, 64 migrations. Most primary keys are ULIDs; Module, Category and Voice use natural keys.

blocks.caption: The core is three domains: `catalog` (Module is the hub), `session` (one run, holding the lineage) and `profile`. Every other domain adds tables and points back to Module; links between domains are few. Domain names follow the `models/` package the author is splitting `models.py` into (not yet committed).
blocks.ascii:
CORE ─ profile ◀─ session ─▶ catalog (Module = the hub)
         ▲          ▲  ▲
   forecast    planner  must_win_goal ─▶ focus          (linked to a run)
   learning_os ◀─ event_reasoning   training · decision · paragraph   (engine domains)
        ▼            ↘
   knowledge         agent   ebook ─▶ canonical ◀─ assistant          (sources, assistants)
Every domain table has an FK to Module.

head: Domain
Entities
Worth knowing
rows: Category, Tag, Voice, Profile, **Module**, ResearchTopic, **Session**, Message, Report, Note, LearningPoint, PeriodSummary, TurnLatency
Session is the hub: it links Module, Profile, topic, forecast run, source session and follow-up parent. Report is one-to-one with Session.
Point carries `dedup_key` and `raw_hash`; extraction reruns only when the hash changes.
Lenses run blind of any Outcome.
Goal, PlanItem, GoalRelation, GoalSource, FocusGoal, FocusGoalTask, FocusContextLog
A GoalSource points to exactly one of: a research topic or a session.
LearningProfile, Concept, ConceptRelation, Indicator, Hypothesis, Evidence, ChangeItem, InboxItem, LearningSession, CadenceReview, ModelVersion…
A hypothesis needs invalidation conditions to leave draft; ModelVersion snapshots the confirmed model.
ReasoningEvent, Run, Node, Edge, TransmissionChain, ReasoningLaw, AssetImpact, NetImpact, Prediction, RealityObservation, VerificationResult
A law's score moves only on a VerificationResult; a failure revises its conditions and never deletes it.
Decision, DecisionLayer, DecisionEvent, DecisionCheckpoint, DecisionAiRun, TrainingCase, TrainingSession, Drill, MasteryState
DecisionAiRun is deliberately not a Session, so it does not skew session counts and cost.
The log is append-only, numbered by `seq`.
SourceDocument, SourceSection, SourceChunk, ConceptLesson, CanonicalModel, CanonicalConcept, Artifact, Implementation, AssessmentItem, ConceptProgress, LearningMemory…
Models are versioned, never edited in place; cache keys include the prompt and model versions.
EbookBook, EbookChapter, EbookChapterState, EbookStatusEvent, Paragraph, ParagraphSentence
Chapter state is kept apart from structure so a re-index never loses progress.
AiAgentProfile, ModuleAgentConfig, SiteAgentConfig, AgentTool, AssistantThread, AssistantMessage, AssistantToolCall

Tools come in 3 kinds: service (registered in code), graphql (read-only), http (GET). SiteAgentConfig is one row: on/off, prompt, mask rules, excluded modules, hints. AssistantMessage keeps `run_meta` and the validated `links`.

sections.title: Frontend
sections.intro: Next.js 16 with thin routes; data through urql + Graphcache with typed documents generated from the SDL.

head: Route
Screen

items.title: Three component layers
items.text: **Atoms** (~150 files, most with stories): props only, no GraphQL. **Workflows** per kind: hold state and fetch data. **Route shells**: thin, just look up the kind and render.

items.title: Data layer
items.text: Codegen reads the committed SDL and writes a `.generated.ts` next to each per-domain `.graphql`. Not client-preset, because it pulled all ~350 documents (757 KB) into one import.

items.title: The cache owns writes
items.text: 18 per-domain update maps, `invalidateQuery` / `invalidateEntity` instead of refetching after a mutation. Types with no `id` get generated null keys, removing ~500 warnings.

items.title: One content surface
items.text: `?surface=drawer|popup&business=…&business-id=…`: one controller opens the same content as a drawer, a popup or its own page.

items.title: Rendering structured output
items.text: `StructuredReport` reads the schema only for labels and order, and picks a widget from each value. Metaphysics has its own chart registry (Purple Star chart, four pillars, hexagrams…).

items.title: PWA, mobile, bundles
items.text: Serwist, switched on by `PT_PWA_ENABLED`. 22 routes checked at 390/768/1440 px. Bundle splitting took `layout.js` from 16.5 MB to 0.82 MB.

blocks.text: There is no global state library. State lives in Graphcache's normalized cache, in the URL (filters, surface, `?s=`), in `useState`, and in localStorage for view preferences.

sections.title: UzAI: study assistant and site guide
sections.intro: One assistant, two surfaces. Inside a lesson, UzAI calls tools to explain. On every other page it only points the way: it returns links to existing modules and never does a module's work itself.

head: Surface
Where
Returns
Limits
rows: Beside a lesson of the AI learning framework
An answer, possibly after a few tool rounds (sources, concepts, book outline, quiz results)
A cap on rounds; long content such as `lesson.artifact` is read page by page (offset)
A floating button on every page, except pages that mount their own assistant
One `bridge.oneshot` call, no tool loop, no data lookups, never runs a module
blocks.note: Both share `AssistantThread`; a `surface` column tells them apart, and a CHECK constraint makes a `lesson` thread have a lesson and a `site` thread have none.

blocks.caption: The safe flow borrowed from the Moza admin assistant: mask before the LLM boundary, and build links from the catalog, never from the model. The example is a health question routed to `dongy_triage`; the onset date leaves the browser only as `<DATE_1>`.
blocks.ascii:
BROWSER (real values)               SERVER (tokens)                     MODEL (tokens + catalog)
1 type: đau đầu, sốt nhẹ từ 12/10/2026
2 mask: … từ <DATE_1>  ──────────▶  3 re-check: raw value → refused ───▶  4 receives masked question + catalog
  sessionStorage: <DATE_1>=12/10/2026                                               │
7 unmask, open prefilled form ◀────  6 check module/field/substring, build ◀── 5 picks dongy_triage,
  the user still presses Run           /m/dongy_triage?f.started_when=<DATE_1>     started_when=<DATE_1>
Variant, value missing: model leaves it out → no placeholder in the link → the user types it in the module's form

items.title: Private values never leave the browser
fields: A mask rule must behave the same in JS and Python (JS syntax, ASCII semantics, no empty matches). If the stored rule set no longer parses, the router turns OFF rather than letting a question through unchecked.

With `\b` around numbers, `_` counts as a word character, so `<PHONE_0901234567>` would smuggle a raw phone number past the check. That is why the rules use digit lookarounds and token indexes are capped at 4 digits.

items.title: Measured by an eval, not by feel
fields: `manage.py eval_site_router` runs 20 real questions through the same code as the mutation, with no DB writes; 5 are held out and never used to tune `hints`. `eval_assistant` does the same for UzAI inside lessons.
On 2026-10-16: 20/20 hits, 5/5 on the held-out set, and the first link was right 18/20 times.

sections.title: Operations: sessions, cleanup, accounts
sections.intro: Who moves a session's state, and how the system heals itself.

blocks.caption: Spawn moves a session to active; a close, a lost tmux or idleness move it to closed. A session closed for idleness whose tmux is still alive revives when someone subscribes.
blocks.ascii:
provisioning --spawn ok--> active --close / tmux_gone / idle_ttl--> closed
     |                       |                                     |
 bridge error        reconcileSessions              revive: idle_ttl + tmux alive → active
     v                       v
   error                   lost
provisioning --oneshot done, or reaper provisioning_timeout (no lease)--> closed

items.title: B1 · Soft close
items.text: ACTIVE idle over 60 minutes → `idle_ttl`. PROVISIONING over 5 minutes with no lease → `provisioning_timeout`. tmux and Claude stay alive.

items.title: B2 · Revive
items.text: On subscribe, if a session closed for idleness and its tmux is alive, the row goes back to ACTIVE and the tailer restarts.

items.title: B3 · Hard reap
items.text: Kill tmux sessions that have no DB row, closed on timeout, or closed more than 1440 minutes ago.

blocks.text:
**Health.** `/livez` checks only the DB and Redis. It is the api container's healthcheck, which the three loop containers wait on, so they start even while the shim on the host is down. `/healthz` adds `bridge doctor` and is for monitoring (`make healthz`). Compose checks `pg_isready` and `redis-cli ping` for db and redis.

**Accounts.** Claude Code stores its OAuth grant per `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in the macOS keychain. The bridge reads the status without refreshing the token, syncs grants between directories, and runs sign-in in its own tmux session, opening the URL in the right browser profile. Before every `spawn`, a pre-flight check blocks a new session if the grant has expired.

**Tests.** Bats for the bridge (`make test-bridge`): doctor, every subcommand, JSONL parsing, one-shot profiles, accounts, ebook, akm, and the kind-list comparison. Pytest for the API inside the container.

sections.title: Admin: settings and troubleshooting
sections.intro: Each setting starts in a file, is edited in one tab, and is read back by one part of the code. The operating pages use the same data to find faults.

blocks.caption: Four tabs write the DB and are seeded only once from YAML (insert-only), so admin edits are never overwritten by a seed. Bridge and Infra are read-only; Credentials acts on the host keychain through the bridge.
blocks.ascii:
SOURCE                     /admin/settings TAB              READ BY
modules/*.yaml        ──▶  Modules (writes DB)        ──▶  /m/[module], engines, Raycast, UzAI
modules/_meta.yaml    ──▶  Categories (writes DB)     ──▶  catalog groups
agents.yaml           ──▶  AI agent (writes DB)       ──▶  UzAI lesson + site router
voices.yaml           ──▶  Voice (writes DB)          ──▶  bridge say
keychain              ──▶  Credentials (via bridge)   ──▶  login check before spawn
bridge/settings.json  ──▶  Bridge (read-only, doctor) ──▶  phantinh-bridge
.env · compose        ──▶  Infra (read-only)          ──▶  api settings
OPERATE: /admin/sessions (close, delete, reconcile, quality) · /admin/performance (TurnLatency)

blocks.text: **A session's quality score.** `/admin/sessions` scores each session green, amber or red. Red when the session is in ERROR, a turn has been stuck mid-stream for over 5 minutes, the report failed schema validation, or the JSONL transcript has more turns than the DB (sync drift). Amber for any other issue: bridge errors, closed with no report, average TTFT over 30 s, a very short session.

blocks.caption: Almost every step lives in admin. The exception is `reingest_session`: a `manage.py` command that replays the transcript into the DB, safe to rerun because every write is idempotent.
blocks.ascii:
Chat won't start        → Bridge tab (doctor)        → SHIM_UNREACHABLE / SHIM_REFUSED → start the shim, same token
Spawn blocked by login  → Credentials tab            → CLAUDE_LOGIN_EXPIRED           → sync the grant / log in
Sent, but no reply      → Sessions · quality         → stuck stream, sync drift       → CLI reingest_session <sid>
List and tmux disagree  → Sessions · Reconcile       → DB orphans / tmux orphans      → Apply fix
One-shot never ends     → Sessions · Running         → > 5 min no lease / TIMEOUT     → reaper closes it; run again
Answers are slow        → Performance                → model/proxy/ingest/tool stage  → fix the slow stage
Report missing/invalid  → Sessions · Modules         → no report / schema errors      → fix schema, preview

sections.title: Design principles
sections.intro: Invariants read from the code and plans, each held by a test or a docstring.

items: **The DB is authoritative; YAML is only a seed.** Config is read per request from the Module row and degrades to named defaults instead of raising, so a half-edited config never makes a page return 500.
**The host does what the container cannot.** tmux, git worktrees, book files, PDFs, `say` and AKM transcripts all go through the bridge.
**One protocol, defined once** in `shared/protocol`, shared by the bridge and the API.
**Ingestion can always resume.** The cursor advances only after writes land; every write is idempotent.
**Redis holds live state, Postgres holds durable state.**
**One door into one-shot runs, one concurrency cap.** Retries keep the lineage; a refused run becomes a re-runnable ERROR row.
**Pure cores, thin resolvers.** reasoning, training, decision, canonical, paragraph, ebook and mustwin never touch the ORM and are unit-tested.
**Check structure; don't copy the parsers' rules.**

**Security lives in code.** CLI permissions come from profiles, extra args pass an allowlist; the shim requires a local Host or a token; private values are masked before they reach the model; the must-win guard code is checked in the API, fails closed and covers respawn; the runtime snapshot never stores `env`; UzAI's tool scope is enforced by code.
